analysis.investment_thesis: CIE Automotive India is a clean-balance-sheet auto components supplier, but with 6.5% revenue CAGR, 11.8% ROE, and an ICE-heavy product portfolio facing EV disruption, it lacks the steady compounding qualities I seek. At 22.5x P/E for this growth and return profile, the price is not compelling.
key_strengths: Debt/Equity of 0.06 — borrowings slashed from ₹1,648 Cr (2020) to ₹426 Cr (2025), balance sheet is clean
OCF positive all 5 years; FCF of ₹885 Cr in 2025 gives ~4.8% yield on market cap
Promoter holding stable at 65.7%, well above my 55% threshold
key_risks: ICE-heavy products (crankshafts, CV joints, gear shafts) face structural EV disruption risk — this is the single biggest concern
Revenue CAGR of only 6.5% over 9 years; FY2025 revenue of ₹9,406 Cr is barely above FY2019's ₹7,908 Cr — flat in real terms
Earnings are wildly volatile: ₹498 Cr (2018) → ₹106 Cr (2020) → -₹136 Cr (2022) → ₹1,125 Cr (2023) → ₹828 Cr (2025) — driven by large exceptional items in 'other income'
red_flags: ROE of 11.8% is well below my 15% minimum threshold — capital is not being deployed productively
Other income swings: -₹749 Cr in 2022 (wiping out profit) and +₹409 Cr in 2023 (inflating earnings) — reported profits are not clean operating earnings
Foreign parent (Spanish promoter) creates related-party and governance opacity risks
P/E of 22.5x is above my 12-20x range for a business with sub-7% revenue growth and an uncertain structural future
analysis.detailed_analysis:
This is a B2B industrial supplier to OEMs — not a consumer-facing business, not FMCG, not financial services. That alone puts it outside my circle of competence and preferred hunting ground. When I look at the numbers, the balance sheet is genuinely good — debt cut by 74% in 5 years is disciplined management — but the income statement tells a different story. Revenue has grown at just 6.5% CAGR over 9 years; adjusting for inflation, the business is essentially treading water. ROE of 11.8% and ROCE of 14.7% indicate that despite clean leverage, this is not a high-quality business earning exceptional returns on capital. Operating margins at 8.2% are thin and leave little buffer in a downcycle.

The earnings history is the biggest disqualifier for me. I need predictable, consistent profit growth — that is how I can estimate intrinsic value with confidence. CIE's net profit has gone from ₹498 Cr to ₹106 Cr to a loss of ₹136 Cr to ₹1,125 Cr in four consecutive years. Much of this volatility is driven by large exceptional items in "other income," meaning reported profits do not reflect true operating earnings power. On top of that, the product portfolio — crankshafts, CV joints, ICE-specific forgings — is directly in the path of EV disruption. I would rather hold cash than own a good balance sheet that is attached to a shrinking end-market. At 22.5x earnings, the market is not pricing in this risk adequately.
